seo_title: The Bremen Town Musicians: Story and Lessons — A Grimm Tale of Teamwork
meta_description: The Bremen Town Musicians story and its lessons, the original Brothers Grimm tale, plus read-aloud tips for teaching your child teamwork and courage. A classic fairy tale guide for ages 4-7.

content.alt: The Bremen Town Musicians - What kind of story is it?
content.text:
What kind of story is The Bremen Town Musicians?

The Bremen Town Musicians is the story of a donkey, a hound, a cat, and a rooster — all cast out for being old and useless — who join forces to find a new life. It's a Brothers Grimm tale that lets children learn, while cheerfully imitating each animal, that every living thing has the right to dream.

content.alt: The Bremen Town Musicians - The original story
content.text:
The original story of The Bremen Town Musicians

This is a tale collected by Germany's Brothers Grimm and included in the second edition of their "Children's and Household Tales" in 1819 (Aarne-Thompson type 130). In the German city of Bremen stands a world-famous tourist landmark: a statue of the four animals climbing on one another's backs.

content.alt: The Bremen Town Musicians - Plot summary
content.text:
Plot summary of The Bremen Town Musicians

A donkey about to be thrown out sets off with a dream of becoming a musician, meeting an old hound, a gloomy cat, and a crowing rooster one by one along the way. Discovering robbers in a house deep in the woods, the four friends climb on one another's backs and cry out so loudly that they drive the robbers away, and they go on to live happily in that house.

content.alt: The Bremen Town Musicians - The lesson it teaches
content.text:
The lesson The Bremen Town Musicians teaches

The heart of the story is that being old or weak doesn't make you useless, and there's great value in the teamwork of filling in one another's gaps to forge a new path. It cheerfully shares the courage to keep moving toward a dream.

content.alt: The Bremen Town Musicians - How to read it aloud
content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Change your voice for each animal — deep and low for the donkey, short and thumping for the dog, thin and sharp for the cat, high and booming for the rooster. In the chorus scene where they scare off the robbers, it's fun to join in and make the animal sounds together with your child. It's well suited to ages 4-7.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is The Bremen Town Musicians best for?
A. It's well suited to ages 4-7. With its fun themes of imitating animal sounds and teamwork, it's great for interactive read-alouds.

Q. Do the four animals ever reach Bremen?
A. Actually, they find happiness in the house in the woods and never make it all the way to Bremen. Part of the charm is that "the journey toward a dream itself became a new life."

Q. What activities pair well with it?
A. A chorus of the four animal sounds, making animal masks, and a chat about "helping friends with what I'm good at" are all great.
